newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures soar on bond, tech strength.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures soar on bond, tech strength.

text.p: September S&P 500 stock index futures registered their second record-high close in two days, aided by dramatic gains in the technology sector and a rally in bonds.
September S&Ps set a new all-time high of 946.75 after stair-stepping higher throughout the day before finishing at a new settlement high of 942.30.

Technology stocks were the driving force, traders and analysts said. The Nasdaq composite index posted a record single-day gain of 38.5 points to end at 1581 as Microsoft shares soared in anticipation of Thursday's earnings release.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average eclipsed 8,000 and kept going, ending 63 points higher at 8,039, despite a selloff in Eastman Kodak Co shares on disappointing second-quarter earnings.
"You can imagine where we'd be if Eastman Kodak wasn't down," said Donald Selkin, head of stock index futures trading at Prudential Securities Inc.
Stock index futures got an early lift from a spike up in Treasury bonds, which were cheered by mild inflation news. The September bond futures contract ended the day 24/32 higher at 114-22/32.

The consumer price index rose a meager 0.1 percent in June, both overall and in the core index excluding food and energy. Analysts had forecast a gain of 0.2 percent in both the overall and core inflation rates.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year cash bond slipped below 6.50 percent, an important psychological barrier, and stuck, traders noted. It ended the day at 6.48 percent.
Stock index futures' gains accelerated in typical fashion after the 1500 EDT close of bond futures trading.
Selkin said the Friday expiration of July stock index and stock options contracts likely aided the equities rally.
